security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate WeChat publishing purpose, but it uses high-risk local automation, browser control, clipboard access, and external commands. Most regex, SVG, and keyword alerts are false positives; the agent-browser execSync wrapper and remote rendering paths remain real security risks. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Shell command construction in agent-browser wrapper
remediation.suggestion: Replace execSync string commands with spawnSync argument arrays. Validate and quote user titles, content, refs, and paths before any command boundary.

remediation.issue: Remote renderer imports and unsanitized SVG insertion
remediation.suggestion: Bundle highlight languages locally, disable remote imports by default, and sanitize fetched SVG before inserting it into the DOM.

remediation.issue: Persistent browser profile keeps WeChat session data
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated profile directory, document session storage clearly, and offer an isolated temporary profile option for sensitive environments.
Require explicit user confirmation before sending system keystrokes or saving drafts, and provide a dry-run mode for preview-only operation.

content.value_statement: Preparing WeChat Official Account drafts from Markdown and images is repetitive. This skill converts content and drives Chrome to compose drafts.
actual_capabilities: Converts Markdown into WeChat-ready HTML with selectable themes.
Creates image-text posts with titles, content, and multiple images.
Uses Chrome CDP or agent-browser to fill WeChat editors.
Copies images and rich HTML through platform clipboard tools.
Preserves a browser profile for WeChat login sessions.
Saves drafts when the submit option is requested.
limitations: Requires Chrome, Bun, and a manual WeChat login.
Uses local OS automation and clipboard permissions.
Markdown rendering can fetch remote images and diagram resources.
Depends on WeChat page structure and account permissions.

use_cases.description: Assemble image-text updates with compressed titles and content for Official Account workflows.

use_cases.description: Exercise Chrome CDP posting flows against WeChat while keeping the browser open for inspection.

best_practices: Review the WeChat draft in Chrome before saving or publishing.
Use a dedicated browser profile for this automation.
Run the skill only with trusted Markdown, images, and paths.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted Markdown that contains remote diagrams.
Do not pass shell metacharacters in titles, content, or paths.
Do not share the persistent browser profile directory.

faq.question: Does this publish directly to WeChat?
faq.answer: It composes drafts and can save them when requested. Users should review drafts in WeChat before publishing.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Chrome and Bun are required. Some clipboard actions also need platform tools or OS permissions.

faq.question: Can it handle Markdown images?
faq.answer: Yes. It replaces Markdown image references with placeholders, then inserts the actual images in the editor.

faq.question: Does it store WeChat credentials?
faq.answer: It keeps a Chrome profile to preserve login sessions. The user controls that profile directory.

faq.question: Can it use different article styles?
faq.answer: Yes. The renderer supports default, grace, and simple themes for Markdown articles.

faq.question: Is it safe with untrusted content?
faq.answer: No. Treat Markdown, image paths, and remote diagrams as trusted inputs only.
